name: apply_patch
description: Apply SMALL localized edits to existing files (one file, a few hunks per call). Supports line replacement, patch envelopes, and unified diffs.
first_use_guidance:
Guidance for later patches in this turn:
- Keep each patch small: one file, a few hunks, minimal context. Split larger edits into sequential calls; never batch many files/hunks to 'save rounds'.
- Copy source text exactly without `read_file` line prefixes; context lines must match.
- For a single-line change prefer `*** Replace in line: <path>` (top-level section, fields per schema).
- When a hunk fails to match, the error echoes the current file text in a `<<<PATCH_TEXT` block; rebuild the patch from that block instead of re-reading the file.
- `*** Add File:` takes `+`-prefixed content; every `*** ...` header opens a new top-level section and is never nested.
- Multi-file unified diffs split automatically, but unified diffs cannot delete files.

file_path.description: Absolute target for a single-file unified diff when its headers omit the file; `path` is an alias.

patch.description: Inline edit in exactly one form: `*** Replace in line:` inside a `*** Begin Patch` envelope; an envelope with `*** Update/Add/Delete File:` sections and `@@` hunks; or a unified diff. No Markdown fences or no-op edits. `*** Replace in line:` takes three single-line fields: `anchor:` (unique substring of the target line), `old:` (exact substring to replace), `new:` (replacement; empty deletes `old`); for whole-line edits use a `*** Update File:` hunk with `@@`. Limit 8000 chars - split larger edits or pass a large patch via `patch_file`.

patch_file.description: Path to a file containing a large patch; must be session-temp or under the working directory. Mutually exclusive with `patch`. Limit 64000 characters.
